newsitem.title: UK: Values set to slip in sleepy N. Sea crude market.
newsitem.headline: Values set to slip in sleepy N. Sea crude market.

text.p: North Sea crude markets were sleepy on Friday, after the previous day's sharp fall in outright values, with sellers under pressure to let differentials slide, traders said.

Cash markets were slightly weaker as sentiment turned negative, but little business was being done. August IPE Brent at 1235 GMT was trading down some 15 cents from the $18.21 close after Thursday's sharp fall.
The U.S. Independence Day holiday and a trade stalemate meant most players would be doing paperwork or lunch.
"We need someone to make the first move (on North Sea crudes) but I'm not sure we'll see it today," said one trader. "Some of the sellers will have to accept lower numbers."
With most of July North Sea crude requirements covered, buyers were waiting for clarification on the timing of Iraqi of exports and the pressure of poor refinery margins to ease.
"The talks right now are for late July and early August and with the uncertainty over Iraq and on margins buyers just wonder why they should do anything now," said one broker.
He pointed to a cross-month Ekofisk traded on Thursday at dated Brent -16 cents as evidence of weaker differentials ahead.
Poor margins were also deterring buyers of Russian Urals in the Mediterranean and depressing its value, despite a tight market for sour crudes.
Wet Brent was pegged at five cents below August in Europe though nothing was heard discussed. Three cargoes were turning wet, with loading dates of July 19-21, 20-22 and 21-23.
Traders said they were beginning to look beyond short-term tightness to the gloomy long-term supply picture.

OPEC output fell in June for the second month in succession, to 26.39 million barrels per day, but due to the absence of Iraqi barrels rather than voluntary production restraint, a Reuters survey showed.
With the return of Iraqi crude in August and scepticism over last week's pledge by OPEC members to keep output within quota, world crude markets look well supplied in the third quarter.
One forward cargo for August was heard traded at $18.20 between two majors.
Intermonth spreads were slightly softer, with Jul/Aug talked lower at +15/+25 from the overnight +20/+30. Aug/Sept and Sept/Oct drifted a cent or so lower at -12/-10 cents and -16/13 cents.
Short-term swaps slipped from early values, with next week at -3/+3 cent against August and the following week (July 14-18) pegged at 26 cents below September.
A July 11-13 Urals cargo was heard done p+c on Thursday, leaving only two or three large Russian cargoes loading in July.
But despite Thursday's sharp fall in underlying Brent futures, margins were still poor at simple processing plants.
Refiners said they were running enough crude to cover their essential sales commitments but no more.
Offers of sweet West African grades met a cool reception, while Libyan Es Sider and Algerian Saharan were also on offer.
-- Sean Maguire, Rosalind Russell +44 171 542 8060
